messages.text:
"An Astra AI based conversation dating Sim that has a customizable anime character 
And when player opens the app it just pops the player's character on the screen and the character also reacts to what the player sees 
This does need a permission from the player to overlay the game though so we should add that in there too 
And camera and microphone permission to video calls and facial expression detection 
So can you do that? (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Built **Moonlit**, a complete, responsive 2D anime dating sim for phones and tablets.

You can customize Astra’s name, hair, outfit, and eyes; progress through branching conversations; build your connection; and collect story memories saved on your device. There’s also an optional in-game floating companion with an opt-in prompt, plus a video-date screen that requests camera and microphone access only when you start a call.

**Privacy note:** A browser game can’t overlay other apps or see what’s on the player’s screen. This prototype keeps the companion within the game. Camera video stays local, and facial-expression detection isn’t implemented; players can choose a feeling during a call to prompt Astra’s reaction.

Validation: `node --check game.js` passed, and I reviewed desktop and mobile screenshots. Start it with `./start.sh` in the project environment.
